steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: So, you got a problem with knowing Kafka or something?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No. I have no problem with knowing her. It's...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: After I got to know her, I always hoped she'd be able to live a normal life. To never have to do those... things she used to.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I introduced her to what work I could. I even wanted her to get a job with Rhine Lab. That didn't pan out, in the end.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But no matter what, the entire time, I've been hoping for a better life for Kafka. I've been hoping for a better her. And that 'better' was based on my standard of living at Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Mm... well, I reckon life at Rhine Lab's not bad, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It was conditional on us not knowing just what we were doing.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But as research workers, we should be pretty first-place for knowing what we're doing, right?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, I don't mean in terms of research goals. I mean what was looming in the background.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If our research would have some adverse effect if it truly succeeded; if our results would be appropriated for something; whether or not that happens to be what we're researching right now.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Since the 'Diαbolic Crisis,' what's been happening inside the company has had me starting to consider this.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I, like you, like a majority of our colleagues, believed that our research was right. That our direction was ideal.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But is that really how things are?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ifrit has given me considerable doubts.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That seed of doubt compelled me to leave Rhine Lab for the time being. To head for Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: So this is what's been on your mind all this time, Silence...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: During my time with Rhodes Island, I've continued my research. But on the flipside, I've begun to pay attention to some data I'd never paid mind before.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: My mentor gave me these data. I never before understood what purpose he had in handing me company and local data, and I'd long since put them aside.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But once I began analysis and research on these data, I came to all sorts of questions about them.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: After I first uncovered those questions, I struggled to sleep again.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Are you talking about things to do with Anthony?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No, Anthony—more precisely, Simon Co.'s affairs were just one part amongst them. A tiny part, even.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There are so many more things going on, not just at Rhine Lab, but throughout the whole of Columbia.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It was only then I truly realized. I understood far too little about this company I called Rhine Lab. This country I called Columbia.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I did not resign myself. I don't believe what happened to Ifrit, or what happened to Anthony, should be considered the norm.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And that's why I involved myself in Anthony's affairs here.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But... perhaps, all at once, I've jumped too far.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I feel the same now as I did then, that moment when Saria emerged from the experiment site with Ifrit cradled unconscious in her arms. As if I have been doused, from the head down, in ice-cold water.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Just what happened in that experiment?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I always thought I knew what I was doing, but now I realize: I really don't know.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I only know that I can never let Ifrit be treated like that again.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This, probably, is the only thing I am capable of persisting in now.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Silence, you're a little drunk. I'll go get you some tea. Sober you up.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Nmm...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'm sorry. Silence. I don't know how to comfort you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's not your fault, Mayer.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I only blame ignorance of my own past.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Personally, I think you already know a hell of a lot, Silence. Just, everyone's got things they're not good at.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mayer. Know this. I truly have not resigned myself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If I'd come to know more, if I'd come to know earlier, perhaps things wouldn't have become the way they are now.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But it's not too late to learn things now, yeah?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I think Director Muelsyse oughta reckon you're pretty strong, too.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'm gonna tell the truth, Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You tell me.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I feel like some bits of you resemble a few colleagues I have.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You learn something you didn't know before, and you feel like everything you learned already was completely pointless. Then you start grieving about, like, why you didn't get the chance to learn this all earlier.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'm not saying that's, like, incorrect, but I think it's a really boring way of going at it. What, everything you put in effort before's just useless? Just like that? Stuff's good for you just 'cause it's new?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Cause if it really is, if you really feel like you can use it, then just go study it with the same effort you put in all those times before, right? It's not like you gotta rush for it.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Here. Drink this up. Tea for the mind.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Things are different, though. These matters aren't the same as academia...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But... but there's sense in what you say, too, I admit...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Aw, jeez. Fine, I'll come over and feed you. Honestly, Silence, you've got zero alcohol tolerance.

a.text: Mayer props up Silence, who's almost lying on the table, and bit by bit, feeds some sobering tea into her mouth.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: How's that? Feel a little better?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Hff... phew...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Much better. Thank you, Mayer.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: If you feel like things are too rough, we can just head straight back?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: No. It's not quite the time yet.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You're gonna keep chatting with Director Muelsyse?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: That's my Silence. Pulling yourself together in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I haven't, not at all.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'd love to run away right now. Run, and head straight back.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But this is a very rare opportunity. Even if it hurts me, I have to see this through to the end.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: What you said might not be a solution to my current issues, but there is one part I believe to be very on point.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I can only learn—accept—all this new knowledge with the same effort I've had in the past.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: However. I also need to make some additional preparations.
